review_scope: Full 94-line definition article read. Twenty-six reference assertions retain version/entitlement/creator restrictions, scope-specific dry runs, publishing versus optional push enablement and post-creation coverage. New details/results/selection/process/AI feature dependencies remain unresolved; no complete-artifact accounting, rights, adoption or native receipt.

claims.statement: Custom-pattern definition depends on product entitlement and actor permission fragments; metadata alone is not effective access.
The article declares fpt, GHES and ghec versions; included feature conditions still constrain particular operations.
AI-assisted regex generation is feature-conditioned and delegates to a separate generation procedure; it is not unconditional availability.
AI generation accepts a text description of the desired detection pattern.
Optional example strings can guide generation; example content is not detection-recall evidence or authorization to submit real secrets.
Repository custom-pattern definition requires Secret Protection enabled on that repository.
Repository pattern creation uses a new-pattern operation and a separate pattern-details fragment, not existing-pattern enablement.
Repository dry runs identify matches without generating alerts; absence of alerts during this test is expected, not no-match proof.
Push protection for the newly defined repository pattern is optional and separately enabled.
The repository Enable button is unavailable until the dry run succeeds and the pattern is published; publication and enforcement are distinct states.
Post-creation repository scanning behavior is delegated to another reusable, not fully specified by this article.
Organization definition requires secret scanning enabled for the repositories intended to be scanned.
Security configurations are described as a way to enable scanning across organization repositories; this is not estate-wide mutation approval.
Organization dry runs target selected repositories without creating alerts, not necessarily the full organization.
Organization push protection is optionally enabled and subject to a separate publication/scope/disruption note.
The organization post-creation description includes complete Git history on all branches; target selection and actual scan completion still require independent evidence.
Organization owners and repository administrators receive findings and can review alerts in the affected repository; no delivery or access receipt was observed.
The enterprise secret-scanning enablement prerequisite is explicitly under the GHES conditional and must not be silently applied identically to cloud versions.
At enterprise scope only the pattern creator may edit and dry-run the pattern; enterprise ownership alone does not erase this restriction.
Enterprise dry-run permission eligibility delegates to a separately reviewed permission fragment.
Enterprise pattern definition selects Security features and New pattern, then includes separate pattern details.
Enterprise dry runs produce matches without alerts and delegate repository selection to a separate enterprise selection fragment.
Enterprise pattern push protection is optional and subject to its separate prerequisite/disruption note.
Enterprise post-creation scanning is limited to repositories in its organizations with Secret Protection enabled; it is not unconditional whole-estate coverage.
The enterprise post-creation description includes entire Git history on all branches within that eligible repository set.
Organization owners and repository administrators are described as notified and able to review repository alerts; actual notification and access remain unverified.
